Hi Susan / Ryan —

Thanks again for joining the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps around pricing and the batching assumptions we discussed so your engineering/finance teams can assess economics: 

Call highlights (short):
- Workload: ~90% short requests (prompt + <=128 tokens), 10% long context retrievals (up to 2k tokens).
- Expected monthly inference volume: initial pilot 5–15M tokens/month, scale target 1–5B tokens over 12–18 months depending on rollout cadence.
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for short requests; bulk jobs can be slower.
- Concurrency: front-end traffic spikes to ~300 qps peak, average ~40 qps.
- Batching expectation: continuous batching for short requests (steady stream), with ~15–50ms added batching latency typical in our Dedicated configs.

Cost math we discussed (baseline):
- Target unit goal you shared: ~$18–25 per 1M tokens during pilot (we used $20/1M as a shorthand in the call).
- With continuous batching + prefix caching, expected cost reduction of ~25–40% vs naive per-request runs depending on cache hit rate and request size.

Susan — perfect, great context. A few concrete notes answering your asks and outlining the path to sub-$10/1M at scale: 

1) Short path to <$10/1M (high level):
   - Batching & continuous request coalescing: with steady request arrival and ~40–60ms aggregation windows we typically reduce per-token compute by ~20–30% on short prompts.
   - Quantization & model variant routing: routing less-sensitive traffic to an 8-bit quantized variant yields ~1.6–2.2x token cost reduction depending on model family.
   - Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts: if you have a high reuse rate ( > 30% identical prefixes) caching drives additional 30–50% per-token savings for repeat reads.
   - Reserved capacity / committed throughput: reserved Dedicated pools reduce unit compute costs vs on-demand by ~30–45% for committed volumes.

Combined, these levers are additive in many cases and get you into the <$10/1M token band at several hundred million tokens/month — realistic for an enterprise rollout.

2) Pilot quote/assumptions in the attached estimate:
   - Pilot volume: 10M tokens/month assumed
   - Model mix: 70% short variant (quantized candidate), 30% full-quality variant for critical flows
   - Concurrency sizing: nominal 50 qps capacity with ability to burst to 300 qps using transient autoscale
   - Expected avg latency impact: +30–40ms due to batching, p95 still within your 300ms target for short flows

I’ve attached the updated estimate and a short simulator run (see the token_estimate tab for per-scenario $/1M).
[Attachment: RIF_token_estimate_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

3) Ask for your CSV: once we have the sample traffic file we’ll run it through our simulator and return a scenario pack with expected $/1M, p95 latency, and recommended Dedicated sizing.

4) Internal note: looping in Marissa for a pricing band and Lauren for any contractual questions on reserved commits. Dev — please flag any ops constraints if our autoscale assumptions are optimistic.

I’ll follow up with a 1-page summary for leadership that maps the levers to breakpoints (pilot -> scale).
